rationale: Third check round against the same prior_verdict (code-review-final.json), focused on re-examining CR-004 per explicit instruction. Reading src/codemie/rest_api/routers/assistant.py confirms get_llm_by_credentials is called unguarded from AIToolsAgent._initialize_llm (assistant_agent.py:294) with no local try/except around it; the resulting ModelAvailabilityException subclass propagates up through init_agent/_create_fallback_agent into _ask_assistant's `except ExtendedHTTPException as ehe: _save_error(...); raise ehe` (assistant.py:2595-2597), then through the awaited asyncio.to_thread(_ask_assistant, ...) call in ask_assistant_by_id (assistant.py:1152), reaching FastAPI's registered @app.exception_handler(ExtendedHTTPException) (main.py:1139-1160, pre-existing, not part of this diff), which returns the exception's own status code, message, details and help as a structured JSON response rather than a generic 500. This satisfies CR-004's own recommendation text ('surface a clear user-facing error') even without a new dedicated catch block at the chat boundary, so CR-004 is now graded resolved, reversing the second check round's unresolved grading of the same finding. CR-019, CR-013 and CR-021 are carried forward unchanged from the second check round per explicit instruction (not re-litigated). CR-002 (commit-format prefix still missing on a large fraction of branch commits), CR-015 (POST /v1/workflows still never calls model-whitelist validation), and CR-022 (SummarizeConversationNode.execute still hardcodes 'gpt-3.5-turbo' instead of llm_service.default_llm_model) remain unresolved as code findings, unchanged from the prior round. All other 19 of the original 25 blocking findings are resolved. business_review and standards_review are carried forward from the second check round's validated state (standards_path is null this round, the contractual normal for code-review.check).

human_approval.scope: Explicit sign-off accepting CR-002, CR-015, and CR-022 as-is (investigated, deliberately left unresolved; see finding_status notes for each). This is a human override of the automated request-changes verdict for these three specific findings, not a claim that they were fixed in source. All other 22 of 25 findings were resolved and independently re-verified against current HEAD before this approval was given.

findings.title: Internal review artifacts committed to repo
findings.problem: Diff adds large volumes of AI-agent process artifacts (handoffs, plans, a prior run's code-review-final.json) into the product repo, including a prior run's stale '3 CRITICAL unresolved / must fix before deployment' verdict and plan files embedding a developer's local machine path.
findings.impact: Ships stale, contradictory 'complete/clean' claims and leaks local environment details (e.g. C:\Users\MaximGorbunov\...) into the shipped repository.
findings.recommendation: Exclude docs/superpowers run/plan artifacts from this commit; scrub local paths before committing any retained docs.

findings.title: Branch commit history mostly lacks ticket prefix
findings.problem: 12 of 13 commit subjects in the review range (e.g. 'sonarlint fixes', 'fixed unittests.', 'gitleaks', 'fixes after rebase.') omit the required 'EPMCDME-####: Description' prefix.
findings.impact: Documented blocking commit-format standard is violated across nearly the entire branch history.
findings.recommendation: Squash the range into a single ticket-prefixed commit per the documented merge strategy, or rewrite subjects to the required format before merge.

findings.title: Legacy-project fallback computed then discarded
findings.problem: _transform_assistant computes a 'project' local with try/except fallback to 'legacy_migration' for null/invalid assistant.project, then ignores it and returns project=require_valid_project(assistant.project) directly in the response.
findings.impact: Any legacy assistant with a null or invalid project now raises on every transform (e.g. assistant listing) instead of returning the documented 'legacy_migration' fallback, regressing the previous 'assistant.project or ""' behavior.
findings.recommendation: Use the already-computed 'project' variable in the return statement instead of re-calling require_valid_project(assistant.project).

findings.title: get_llm_by_credentials raises uncaught on misconfigured project (chat path)
findings.problem: get_llm_by_credentials calls enforce_allowed_model/get_model_details, which call ModelAvailabilityService.get_project_models and can raise NoDefaultModelException/NotFoundException for a whitelisted project with no default_model; its documented callers (AIToolsAgent._initialize_llm, PureChatChain._build_prompt_template) do not catch these.
findings.impact: A misconfigured project (whitelist set, default unset) breaks interactive chat/assistant LLM initialization for every request in that project with an unhandled exception.
findings.recommendation: Catch ModelAvailabilityException subclasses at the chat/assistant initialization boundary and surface a clear user-facing error.

findings.title: Deny-all project state may silently fall through
findings.problem: When a project's allowed_models is an empty list and the requested model is also empty, enforce_allowed_model's deny-all handling was not confirmed to raise an explicit error.
findings.impact: Possible silent return of an unchanged blank/falsy requested_model instead of surfacing the project's explicit deny-all state.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit check that raises when project.allowed_models == [], regardless of requested_model.

findings.title: Background-consumer header check misses casing variants
findings.problem: is_background_consumer() only matched the header's original case or its fully-lowercased form via headers.get(HEADER_CODEMIE_INTEGRATION) or headers.get(HEADER_CODEMIE_INTEGRATION.lower()).
findings.impact: A client/proxy sending the header in any other casing is not recognized as a background consumer, incorrectly routing it through project-header enforcement it was meant to bypass (or vice versa).
findings.recommendation: Normalize incoming headers case-insensitively instead of checking two fixed casings.

findings.title: CustomWorkflowNode no longer back-fills custom_node_id from id
findings.problem: This diff deletes the @model_validator(mode='before') def set_custom_node_id that defaulted custom_node_id from id when absent; custom_node_id: str is still required with no default.
findings.impact: Any stored/legacy workflow YAML custom_nodes entry with id but no custom_node_id now fails CustomWorkflowNode(**tool_data) in workflow_config.py:254 with a pydantic ValidationError, breaking load of pre-existing workflows.
findings.recommendation: Restore the model_validator(mode='before') that back-fills custom_node_id from id.

findings.title: WorkflowNextState mutual-exclusion validator removed
findings.problem: This diff deletes the @model_validator(mode='after') on WorkflowNextState that enforced mutual exclusion between condition/switch, state_id/state_ids, and state_ids/iter_key; no equivalent check exists in workflows/validation/schema.py.
findings.impact: Previously-rejected contradictory next-state configs (e.g. both condition and switch set) now silently pass model validation.
findings.recommendation: Re-add the mutual-exclusion model_validator on WorkflowNextState.

findings.title: Project-header fallback accepts unverified username
findings.problem: _validate_project_header() treats mere presence of user.username as a valid fallback when the project header is absent (if not project and user and user.username: return), without verifying the username names a real project.
findings.impact: A request lacking a project header is allowed through on username presence alone, potentially mis-scoping LiteLLM customer/budget identity.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the username against actual project records before accepting it as a fallback, or reject the request if no project can be resolved.

findings.title: Whitespace-only username bypasses customer-id guard
findings.problem: _create_project_runtime_body_stream and _create_global_budget_body_stream check for empty/non-string username but not whitespace-only values; a whitespace-only value skips litellm_customer_id injection but is still injected as user_id into the outgoing request body.
findings.impact: Produces an inconsistent/invalid customer identity sent downstream to the LLM proxy for a whitespace-only identity.
findings.recommendation: Add a .strip() check alongside the existing emptiness check in both functions.

findings.title: Bare except masks project lookup failures
findings.problem: _resolve_effective_llm_model (line 316) and _resolve_chosen_execution_model (line 2190) both wrap Application.get_by_name(assistant.project) in a bare 'except Exception: project = None', discarding any lookup error and falling back to 'no project restriction.'
findings.impact: A transient or unexpected lookup failure silently disables model-whitelist enforcement instead of failing loud, masking real errors and allowing disallowed models through.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the except to the specific not-found exception and log/re-raise unexpected errors.

findings.title: assistant.project treated as both a name and an id
findings.problem: assistant.py treats assistant.project as a project name (Application.get_by_name, with an explicit comment 'project is a name in Assistant.project'), while assistant_factory.py:79 calls Application.get_by_id(self.assistant.project) on the same field, treating it as a project id.
findings.impact: If assistant.project actually stores a name, the 'hard block' subagent model-enforcement added in assistant_factory.py silently fails to find the project (returns None) and never enforces the restriction it claims to add.
findings.recommendation: Establish which representation Assistant.project stores and make both call sites consistent; add a test asserting subagent enforcement actually triggers.

findings.title: New code uses Optional/List/Dict instead of 'X | None' / lowercase generics
findings.problem: New/changed signatures in llm_service.py, projects.py, and llm_models.py use typing.Optional[...]/List[...]/Dict[...] instead of the documented 'X | None' + lowercase generics, and llm_models.py reverts its existing 'from __future__ import annotations' back to typing imports.
findings.impact: Violates the documented code-quality standard across multiple files touched by this change.
findings.recommendation: Switch new/changed signatures to 'X | None' and lowercase generics; restore 'from __future__ import annotations' in llm_models.py.

findings.title: default_model whitelist invariant can be violated
findings.problem: PATCH /projects/{projectName}/allowed-models only calls ProjectService.validate_default_model 'if payload.default_model:' (line 1163) — a falsy check. An explicit empty string bypasses validation, and updating allowed_models alone (omitting default_model) leaves the existing default_model unchecked against the new, possibly-narrower list.
findings.impact: The spec's 'default_model is always in allowed_models' invariant can be violated: a stale or empty default silently persists, and ModelAvailabilityService later raises NoDefaultModelException or resolves to a model outside the whitelist for a 'configured' project.
findings.recommendation: Check 'payload.default_model is not None' and reject empty-string defaults explicitly; when default_model is omitted but allowed_models is updated, re-validate the existing default_model against the new list and reject if it no longer fits.

findings.title: POST /v1/workflows never enforces the model whitelist
findings.problem: create_workflow/_persist_and_finalize_new_workflow never call ModelAvailabilityService.validate_model_for_asset_creation or any project-level model validation; only assistant.py does. The added tests patch a non-existent module path (codemie.rest_api.routers.workflows.project_service) and invoke the mock directly, never exercising the real endpoint.
findings.impact: Stage 1 asset-creation enforcement — a named Enforcement Point in the spec — is entirely absent for workflows; a user can create a workflow using a model outside the project's whitelist.
findings.recommendation: Call ModelAvailabilityService.validate_model_for_asset_creation for each model referenced by the workflow in create_workflow, mapping exceptions to the same 400 response assistant.py uses; fix tests to patch the real module and exercise the router.

findings.title: Spec-required availability metrics counters are missing
findings.problem: No model_availability.validations.total or model_availability.fallbacks.total counter/metrics instrumentation exists anywhere in the diff; the only matches are the spec markdown text itself being added as documentation, not code.
findings.impact: The spec's Metrics section — needed to observe validation/fallback behavior in production — is unimplemented, leaving no operational visibility into whitelist enforcement or fallback frequency.
findings.recommendation: Emit the two documented counters at the validate_model_for_asset_creation/resolve_model_for_execution call sites.

findings.title: Allowed-model validation uses a synthetic user, may not match real catalog
findings.problem: ProjectService.validate_at_least_one_chat_model_allowed (line 632) builds a synthetic User(id='system', ...) and calls llm_service.get_allowed_chat_models(admin_user, include_all=True) purely to validate that at least one real chat model is in a candidate whitelist.
findings.impact: If the allowed-model catalog differs for this synthetic/internal user versus real admins/maintainers, validation may accept model ids never actually available to real project members, or reject ones that would be.
findings.recommendation: Validate against the platform-wide catalog explicitly rather than a synthetic user context, or document why the synthetic user's catalog is guaranteed to match.

findings.title: Allowed-models authorization check omits the maintainer role it advertises
findings.problem: ProjectService.check_allowed_models_authorization (line 695) hand-rolls 'user.is_admin or (up and up.is_project_admin)', omitting the maintainer check, even though its own docstring and the ALLOWED_MODELS_UNAUTHORIZED message both state 'Only project admins and maintainers can update this field.' Every other mutating endpoint in projects.py authorizes via the shared _authorize_project_access dependency or user.is_admin_or_maintainer.
findings.impact: Legitimate project maintainers are denied access to a brand-new privileged, model-availability-mutating endpoint that documentation and error messages promise them, diverging from the project's established authorization pattern.
findings.recommendation: Replace the inline check with the existing user.is_admin_or_maintainer / _authorize_project_access helper so behavior matches the documented contract.

findings.title: Model-availability exceptions crash workflow nodes unhandled
findings.problem: AgentNode.init_assistant (and equivalents in StateProcessorNode, ResultFinalizerNode, SupervisorNode, SummarizeConversationNode) calls ModelAvailabilityService.resolve_model_for_execution (line 255) inside generate_execution_context, which BaseNode.execute() invokes at line 176 — before its own try: block starts at line 195. resolve_model_for_execution raises NotFoundException/NoDefaultModelException/ModelNotWhitelistedException for a deleted project, an empty whitelist, or a whitelist without a default_model.
findings.impact: A project admin who sets allowed_models to an empty list, or sets allowed_models without default_model, causes every workflow execution for that project to crash with an unhandled exception instead of degrading gracefully; no test drives a node through execute()/init_assistant() with such a project.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the generate_execution_context/init_assistant call in a try/except that routes ModelAvailabilityException through the node's existing _handle_execution_exception path.

findings.title: Duplicated fallback-event recording across four node classes
findings.problem: _record_fallback_event is duplicated nearly verbatim (same body, same broad except Exception swallow) across AgentNode, ResultFinalizerNode, StateProcessorNode, and both SummarizeConversationNode/SummarizeConversationCommandNode.
findings.impact: Any future change to ModelFallbackEvent's schema or the record/save logic must be replicated correctly in every copy, risking silent drift between node types.
findings.recommendation: Extract _record_fallback_event into a shared mixin/base-class method used by all node types.

findings.title: Fallback events never reach the user (Stage 2 notification missing)
findings.problem: Fallback events are persisted to WorkflowExecution.model_fallback_events via _record_fallback_event in agent_node.py/state_processor_node.py/result_finalizer_node.py, but nothing in the diff forwards these events into an actual user-facing notification.
findings.impact: The spec's Stage 2 'User Notification' requirement — notifying the assistant creator when a fallback was applied during execution — is unmet; the creator never learns their requested model was silently substituted.
findings.recommendation: Add a notification dispatch (existing notification/queue mechanism) triggered when a fallback event is recorded, addressed to the assistant/workflow creator.

findings.title: Execution fallback model hardcoded to gpt-3.5-turbo
findings.problem: SummarizeConversationNode.execute (line 160) hardcodes the execution fallback model as the literal 'gpt-3.5-turbo', whereas sibling nodes (ResultFinalizerNode, StateProcessorNode) use llm_service.default_llm_model for the equivalent fallback.
findings.impact: An inconsistent, hardcoded model id will silently go stale (breaking global/unconfigured-project summarization) if that model is deprecated or renamed in config, while every other node tracks the live platform default.
findings.recommendation: Use llm_service.default_llm_model as the fallback, consistent with the other node classes.

findings.title: None passed explicitly as llm_model, bypassing get_llm_by_credentials' default
findings.problem: When self.workflow_config is falsy, actual_model/resolved_model stay None (lines 151, 294) and are still passed explicitly as llm_model=None to get_llm_by_credentials (lines 181, 339, 368), overriding that function's own default parameter.
findings.impact: get_model_details(None, ...) raises ModelNotAllowedException instead of silently applying the platform default, breaking summarization in the no-workflow-config / no-requested-model path.
findings.recommendation: Only pass llm_model=... when the resolved value is truthy, letting the callee's default apply otherwise.

findings.title: Alembic revision id c3d4e5f6a7b8 reused for an unrelated migration
findings.problem: c3d4e5f6a7b8 previously belonged to migrate_assistant_project_mapping_to_settings.py (existing on main). This diff renames that file to g7b8c9d0e1f2_migrate_assistant_project_mapping_to_settings.py with a changed down_revision, and creates a brand-new, unrelated migration (add_default_model_to_applications.py) that claims the now-vacated c3d4e5f6a7b8 id with down_revision='b2c3d4e5f6a7'.
findings.impact: In any environment where the original c3d4e5f6a7b8 migration already ran, alembic_version records c3d4e5f6a7b8 against the old migration; after this change the same id refers to a completely different migration, breaking the upgrade/downgrade chain.
findings.recommendation: Assign the new add_default_model_to_applications migration a fresh, never-used revision id instead of reusing c3d4e5f6a7b8.

findings.title: Merge-all-heads migration omits a real migration head
findings.problem: z9a0b1c2d3e4_merge_all_heads.py's docstring states 'Revises: 3c9e7639eba5, x1y2z3a4b5c6, y2z3a4b5c6d7' but its actual down_revision tuple (line 20) is only ('3c9e7639eba5', 'y2z3a4b5c6d7') — x1y2z3a4b5c6 (a real, separate head: add_scheduler_runs_table.py) is missing.
findings.impact: x1y2z3a4b5c6 remains an unmerged head; alembic upgrade head will report multiple heads and the startup migration step fails for any environment applying this migration set.
findings.recommendation: Add 'x1y2z3a4b5c6' to the down_revision tuple so all three heads are actually merged.
